title: 1977 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Find the smallest integer \(n\) such that \[ \begin{aligned} (x^2+y^2+z^2)^2 &\le{}\\[-4pt] &n(x^4+y^4+z^4) \end{aligned} \] for all real numbers \(x,\) \(y\) and \(z.\)

solutions.text:
By Cauchy-Schwarz, \[ \begin{aligned} (x^2+y^2+z^2)^2&\le3Q,\\ Q&=x^4+y^4+z^4. \end{aligned} \] Equality occurs when \(x^2=y^2=z^2\ne0,\) so no smaller value can work. Thus the smallest integer is \(3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz to the three numbers \(x^2,\) \(y^2,\) \(z^2\)
Use equal nonzero values of \(x^2,\) \(y^2,\) \(z^2\) to test sharpness
